text.en: The quarterly periodical Ainu Taimuzu is published in the Ainu language simultaneously using two different writing systems ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--the-quarterly-periodical-ainu-taimuzu-is-published-in⟧. Unless otherwise noted, the Ainu examples in this grammar were provided by Shirasawa Nabe and represent the Chitose dialect ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--unless-otherwise-noted-the-ainu-examples-in-this⟧.
text.ja: 季刊誌『アイヌタイムズ』は、2つの異なる表記体系を同時に用いてアイヌ語で刊行されている⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--the-quarterly-periodical-ainu-taimuzu-is-published-in⟧。本稿のアイヌ語の事例は特に断らない限り白沢ナベ氏の教示によるものであり、千歳方言である⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--unless-otherwise-noted-the-ainu-examples-in-this⟧。

text.en: Saru Ainu, spoken along the Saru River basin centered around Biratori, is the most thoroughly described in grammar and has the largest recorded vocabulary of all Ainu dialects ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--saru-ainu-spoken-along-the-saru-river-basin⟧. Kindaichi Kyōsuke's (1931a) 'Yūkara gohō teiyō' was the first grammatical description of Ainu of reference value, and Kindaichi's (1960) 'Ainu-gogaku kōgi' was its revised edition ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--kindaichi-ky-suke-s-1931a-y-kara-goh⟧. Chiri Mashiho's 'Ainu gohō gaisetsu' (1936) was written within the framework of Kindaichi's (1931a) 'Yūkara gohō teiyō' as a comparative study of the Saru dialect described by Kindaichi and the Horobetsu dialect ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--chiri-mashiho-s-ainu-goh-gaisetsu-1936-was⟧. To date, no comprehensive grammar covering Horobetsu Ainu alone has been written ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--to-date-no-comprehensive-grammar-covering-horobetsu-ainu⟧.
text.ja: 平取を中心とする沙流川流域の言葉（沙流方言）は、北海道方言のみならずアイヌ語のすべての方言の中でも、文法が最も精密に記述され、語彙も数多く記録されている⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--saru-ainu-spoken-along-the-saru-river-basin⟧。文法書としては金田一京助（1931a）「ユーカラ語法摘要」が参照する価値のある最初のものであり、その改訂版が金田一（1960）「アイヌ語学講義」である⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--kindaichi-ky-suke-s-1931a-y-kara-goh⟧。知里真志保の『アイヌ語法概説』（1936）は金田一京助の「ユーカラ語法摘要」（1931）の枠組みに沿って書かれ、金田一の記述した沙流方言と幌別方言の対照研究という形になっている⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--chiri-mashiho-s-ainu-goh-gaisetsu-1936-was⟧。幌別方言だけの総合的な文法書は現在まで書かれていない⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--to-date-no-comprehensive-grammar-covering-horobetsu-ainu⟧。

text.en: Murasaki Kyoko authored Karafuto Ainugo: Bunpō-hen (1979), which was the first comprehensive Sakhalin Ainu grammar since Chiri's 1942 study ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--murasaki-kyoko-authored-karafuto-ainugo-bunp-hen-1979⟧. Asai Tōru's sketch 'Ainu-go Ishikari hōgen bumpō no gairyaku' (1969) is the only coherent grammatical description of the Ishikari dialect ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--asai-t-ru-s-sketch-ainu-go-ishikari⟧. Kirsten Refsing's 'The Ainu Language' (1986) is a comprehensive grammar of the Shizunai dialect based on a single speaker, Oda Suteno, and is the first full-scale grammar of Ainu written in English ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--kirsten-refsing-s-the-ainu-language-1986-is⟧.
text.ja: 村崎恭子は1979年に「アイヌ語法研究」以来の樺太方言の文法書である『カラフトアイヌ語――文法編――』を著した⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--murasaki-kyoko-authored-karafuto-ainugo-bunp-hen-1979⟧。石狩方言の文法書としては、浅井亨が『アイヌ民族誌』（1969）に書いた「アイヌ語石狩方言文法の概略」が唯一のまとまったものである⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--asai-t-ru-s-sketch-ainu-go-ishikari⟧。キーステン・レフシンによる『The Ainu Language』（1986）は織田ステノの言葉について文法体系を網羅的に記述したもので、静内方言の最初の文法書であるだけでなく、英語で書かれた初めての本格的なアイヌ語文法書でもある⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--kirsten-refsing-s-the-ainu-language-1986-is⟧。

text.en: Uehara Kumajiro's 1792 vocabulary Moshiogusa, the first Ainu dictionary in the world, contains 2,740 words and served via its German translation as the basis for August Pfizmaier's grammar, the world's first grammar of Ainu ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--moshiogusa-published-in-1792-is-the-first-ainu⟧⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--uehara-kumajiro-s-1792-vocabulary-moshiogusa-contains-2⟧. Around 1824, Uehara Kumajiro compiled a further Ainu vocabulary collection containing approximately 9,380 words ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--around-1824-uehara-kumajiro-compiled-an-ainu-vocabulary⟧. In early Japanese documents recording Ainu, such as Matsumae no kotoba and Ezo-kotoba, Ainu words are written with hiragana including hentaigana ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-the-earliest-japanese-documents-of-ainu-such⟧, and the oldest known record of Ainu written by a Japanese person is 'Matsumae no koto', estimated to have been copied around 1626–1627 ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--the-oldest-known-record-of-ainu-written-by⟧. Girolamo de Angelis's 1624 report contains 34 numerals, 16 nouns, and 2 compound expressions, which is regarded as the world's oldest vocabulary list of the Ainu language ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--girolamo-de-angelis-s-1624-report-contains-34⟧. John Batchelor's 'An Ainu-English-Japanese Dictionary' (1889) was the first full-scale dictionary arranged by headword pronunciation, primarily based on the Saru dialect ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--john-batchelor-s-an-ainu-english-japanese-dictionary⟧. In 1996, 'Kayano Shigeru no Ainu-go jiten' and Tamura Suzuko's 'Ainu-go Saru hōgen jiten' were published successively, making Saru the dialect with the most comprehensive dictionaries ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-1996-kayano-shigeru-no-ainu-go-jiten⟧. Hattori Shirō's (1964) dialect dictionary compiles lexical data across ten dialects: nine surveyed using a common questionnaire (Yakumo, Horobetsu, Saru, Obihiro, Bihoro, Asahikawa, Nayoro, Sōya, and Rayciska Sakhalin) plus Torii Ryūzō's Kuril Ainu recordings ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--hattori-shir-s-1964-dialect-dictionary-compiles-lexical⟧. Chiri Mashiho's 'Bunrui Ainugo Jiten: Shokubutsu-hen' specifies forty-nine localities as collection or usage locations in its explanatory notes ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--chiri-mashiho-s-bunrui-ainugo-jiten-shokubutsu-hen⟧, and his 'Chimei Ainugo Shōjiten' (1956) lists forty-one localities, including broad designations such as Hokkaido ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--chiri-mashiho-s-chimei-ainugo-sh-jiten-1956⟧. Russian naval officer G. I. Davidov compiled an Ainu dictionary containing approximately 2,000 words following his voyages in 1806–1807 ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--russian-naval-officer-g-i-davidov-compiled-an⟧. Mikhail M. Dobrotvorsky's posthumous manuscript was edited by his brother Ivan Dobrotvorsky and published in 1875 as an Ainu-Russian dictionary ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--mikhail-m-dobrotvorsky-s-posthumous-manuscript-was-edited⟧; it contains 10,930 headwords, nearly half of which were compiled from previously published European vocabularies ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--dobrotvorsky-s-ainu-russian-dictionary-contains-10-930⟧, while more than half of the vocabulary (5,733 words by his own count) was recorded directly by himself in the field, making it the largest dictionary of Sakhalin Ainu to date ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--more-than-half-of-the-vocabulary-in-dobrotvorsky⟧. In Dobrotvorsky's (1875) dictionary, only words that Dobrotvorsky recorded himself from first-hand fieldwork are marked with accent ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-dobrotvorskiy-s-1875-dictionary-only-words-that⟧. Stepan P. Krasheninnikov published a 253-word Northern Kuril Ainu vocabulary collected in 1738 on Shumshu and Paramushir in his Description of Kamchatka Land (1755) ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--stepan-p-krasheninnikov-published-a-253-word-northern⟧. Georg W. Steller collected 378 words of Northern Kuril Ainu in 1743, which Heinrich J. Klaproth published in Asia Polyglotta (1823) under the name 'Kamchatka Ainu' ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--georg-w-steller-collected-378-words-of-northern⟧. Benedykt Dybowski's dictionary published in 1891, containing approximately 1,900 words, is the largest vocabulary compiled for North Kuril Ainu ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--benedykt-dybowski-s-dictionary-published-in-1891-containing⟧; Dybowski's Shumshu Kuril vocabulary contains a strikingly disproportionate number of nouns, often derivatives rather than simple basic forms, in relation to other lexical categories ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--dybowski-s-shumshu-kuril-vocabulary-contains-a-strikingly⟧. In 1787, Jean François de La Pérouse visited Tomari-Oro (Kushunnai Bay) on the west coast of Sakhalin and recorded 161 words, which is considered the world's first vocabulary of the Sakhalin dialect ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-1787-jean-fran-ois-de-la-p⟧. In 1872, Alphonse L. Pinart collected 295 Kuril Ainu words from an Aleut speaker, Paul Uiai, in Alaska, which were transcribed and published by Toru Asai in 1974 ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-1872-alphonse-l-pinart-collected-295-kuril⟧. In 1899, Ryuzo Torii conducted research on the language and culture of Kuril Ainu people relocated to Shikotan Island and collected approximately 900 words ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-1899-ryuzo-torii-conducted-research-on-the⟧. Ezo kotoba irohabiki (1848), compiled by Kizaemon Itoya in Otaru, contains forms of an extinct west-coast Hokkaido Ainu dialect arranged by the Japanese Iroha syllabary ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--ezo-kotoba-irohabiki-1848-compiled-by-kizaemon-itoya⟧. Chiri Yukie's 'Ainu Shin'yōshū' (1923) is known as the work of the first Ainu person to print her own language in movable type ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--chiri-yukie-s-ainu-shin-y-sh-1923⟧.
text.ja: 上原熊次郎が1792年にまとめた語彙集『もしほ草』は世界最初のアイヌ語辞典であり⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--moshiogusa-published-in-1792-is-the-first-ainu⟧、2740語を擁し、そのドイツ語訳に基づいてプフィッツマイエルが世界初のアイヌ語文法書を著した⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--uehara-kumajiro-s-1792-vocabulary-moshiogusa-contains-2⟧。上原熊次郎は1824年頃に約9380語を収録した語彙集をさらに編纂した⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--around-1824-uehara-kumajiro-compiled-an-ainu-vocabulary⟧。『松前ノ言葉』や『蝦夷言葉』のような日本の最初期のアイヌ語資料では、アイヌ語も変体仮名を含む平仮名で書かれており⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-the-earliest-japanese-documents-of-ainu-such⟧、日本人による最古のアイヌ語の記録は『松前の言』であり、1626〜1627年頃には成立していたと推定される⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--the-oldest-known-record-of-ainu-written-by⟧。ジロラモ・デ・アンジェリスの1624年の報告書巻末には数詞34語、名詞16語、複合表現2例が挙げられており、世界最古のアイヌ語語彙集とされる⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--girolamo-de-angelis-s-1624-report-contains-34⟧。ジョン・バチェラーの『蝦和英三対辞書』（1889年初版）は本格的な音引き辞書の最初のものであり、沙流方言を中心に編まれたものであった⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--john-batchelor-s-an-ainu-english-japanese-dictionary⟧。1996年に『萱野茂のアイヌ語辞典』と田村すゞ子の『アイヌ語沙流方言辞典』が相次いで刊行され、沙流方言は辞書としても最も充実した方言となった⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-1996-kayano-shigeru-no-ainu-go-jiten⟧。服部四郎編（1964）『アイヌ語方言辞典』は、共通調査票による9方言（八雲、幌別、沙流、帯広、美幌、旭川、名寄、宗谷、樺太ライチシカ）の聞き取りに鳥居龍蔵採録の千島方言語彙を加えた10方言を一覧収録したものである⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--hattori-shir-s-1964-dialect-dictionary-compiles-lexical⟧。知里真志保の『分類アイヌ語辞典 植物編』の凡例には採集地または使用地として49の地名が示されており⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--chiri-mashiho-s-bunrui-ainugo-jiten-shokubutsu-hen⟧、知里真志保（1956a）『地名アイヌ語小辞典』の凡例には「北海道」という広範囲な指定も含めると41の地点が示されている⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--chiri-mashiho-s-chimei-ainugo-sh-jiten-1956⟧。ロシア海軍士官ダヴィドフは、1806〜1807年の航海を経て約2000語に及ぶアイヌ語辞典を作成した⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--russian-naval-officer-g-i-davidov-compiled-an⟧。M・M・ドブロトヴォルスキーの遺稿は兄のイワンによってまとめられ、1875年に『アイヌ語ロシア語辞典』として出版された⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--mikhail-m-dobrotvorsky-s-posthumous-manuscript-was-edited⟧。同辞典の見出し語数は10930語であるが、その半数近くはそれまでにヨーロッパで公刊された語彙集から集められたものであり⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--dobrotvorsky-s-ainu-russian-dictionary-contains-10-930⟧、収録語彙の半数以上（本人記述で5733語）は彼自身が現地で採録したものであり、現在に至るまで樺太アイヌ語の最大の辞書である⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--more-than-half-of-the-vocabulary-in-dobrotvorsky⟧。ドブロトヴォルスキーの辞書（1875）では、彼自身が直接フィールドワークで記録した単語にのみアクセント記号が付されている⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-dobrotvorskiy-s-1875-dictionary-only-words-that⟧。S・P・クラシェニンニコフは、1738年にシュムシュ島・パラムシル島で採録した253語の単語を、1755年の『カムチャッカ地誌』に掲載した⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--stepan-p-krasheninnikov-published-a-253-word-northern⟧。G・W・シュテラーが1743年に北千島で集めたアイヌ語資料は378語を数え、後にクラプロートの『アジア・ポリグロッタ』（1823）に「カムチャッカアイヌ語」として収録された⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--georg-w-steller-collected-378-words-of-northern⟧。ベネディクト・ディボフスキが1891年に公刊した約1900語を採録する辞書は北千島アイヌ語最大の語彙集であり⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--benedykt-dybowski-s-dictionary-published-in-1891-containing⟧、ディボフスキによる占守島千島アイヌ語語彙集は他の品詞に比べて名詞が著しく偏って多く、それらの名詞は単純な基本形よりも派生語であることが多い⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--dybowski-s-shumshu-kuril-vocabulary-contains-a-strikingly⟧。1787年にフランス人のラ・ペルーズが樺太西海岸のクシュンナイ湾を訪れ161語を記録したものが、世界初の樺太方言の語彙集とされている⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-1787-jean-fran-ois-de-la-p⟧。1872年にアルフォンス・L・ピナールがアラスカでアリュート人のポール・ウイアイから聞き取った千島アイヌ語の語彙295語は、浅井亨によって1974年に翻刻された⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-1872-alphonse-l-pinart-collected-295-kuril⟧。1899年に鳥居龍蔵は色丹島で千島アイヌ人の言語と文化についての調査を行い、約900語の語彙を集めた⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-1899-ryuzo-torii-conducted-research-on-the⟧。糸屋喜左衛門が小樽で著した『蝦夷言いろは引』（1848年）には、日本語のいろは順に配列された、絶滅した北海道西海岸方言の形式が含まれている⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--ezo-kotoba-irohabiki-1848-compiled-by-kizaemon-itoya⟧。知里幸恵は『アイヌ神謡集』（1923）によって、アイヌとして初めて自分の言葉であるアイヌ語を活字化した人物として知られている⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--chiri-yukie-s-ainu-shin-y-sh-1923⟧。

text.en: The Ainu language has no indigenous writing system ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--no-indigenous-writing-system⟧, and until modern times the Ainu themselves had no practice of writing their language down in a script ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--until-modern-times-the-ainu-themselves-had-no⟧; Ainu-language texts began to be documented by Ainu people themselves only in the twentieth century ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--ainu-language-texts-began-to-be-documented-by⟧. There are very few reliable and sizable documents of the Ainu language dating back as far as the 17th century or the first half of the 18th century ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--there-are-very-few-reliable-and-sizable-documents⟧. The two words in a record dated 1591 by Morera are most probably the earliest Ainu words ever documented in a Western language ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--the-two-words-in-a-record-dated-1591⟧; in that record, the form *Ainomoxori* represents Ainu *ainu mosir* 'the Ainu country or land' ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-the-early-western-record-by-morera-1591⟧, and the form *Rebuncur* represents Ainu *repun kur* 'alien people from beyond the sea' ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-the-early-western-record-by-morera-1591-2⟧. In the earliest Japanese documents of Ainu, such as Matsumae no kotoba and Ezo-kotoba, Ainu words as well as Japanese are written with hiragana, including hentaigana ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-the-earliest-japanese-documents-of-ainu-such⟧, and the hentaigana characters 川 (*tsu*) and 志 (*shi*) are used more frequently to transcribe Ainu than Japanese in these early documents ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-early-japanese-documents-recording-ainu-the-hentaigana⟧. In later Edo-era documents, Ainu tends to be written with katakana, whereas Japanese is generally written with Chinese characters and hiragana ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-later-edo-era-documents-ainu-tends-to⟧. Bugaeva proposes that the modern Ainu form *iwanpe* 'six' may historically have had a shape like **iwanp* or **iwanpə*, as suggested by the 17th-century kana spelling *yuwanfu* in Matsumae no kotoba ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--the-modern-ainu-form-iwanpe-six-may-historically⟧. Whereas *okkay* in modern Ainu usually means 'adult man', in 17th-century documents such as Angelis's record and Matsumae no kotoba it meant 'young man, boy' ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--whereas-okkay-in-modern-ainu-usually-means-adult⟧. In the early 18th century, the Ainu pronunciation of *hu* was either [hu] or [xu], rather than the modern pronunciation [ɸu] ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-the-early-18th-century-the-ainu-pronunciation⟧. Bugaeva proposes that the root *rep* 'center of hearth or sea' may historically have contained a consonant **H* (**reHp*), as evidenced by the spelling 'あへ連んほう' (*aherenhou*) in Ezo kotoba ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--the-root-rep-center-of-hearth-or-sea⟧. Ezo sōshi (1790) employs the special kana character ト゜ to transcribe the syllable /*tu*/ ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--ezo-s-shi-1790-employs-the-special-kana⟧. Matsumae no kotoba (17th c.) contains kana spellings such as *reira* for modern *réra* 'wind' and *teita* for modern *téta* 'here', suggesting long vowels that are absent in modern Hokkaido Ainu ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--matsumae-no-kotoba-17th-c-contains-kana-spellings⟧. Old Japanese documents frequently record modern Hokkaido Ainu *tókap* 'daytime' with kana spellings indicating a long first syllable, such as *tofukatsufu* or *toogapu* ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--old-japanese-documents-frequently-record-modern-hokkaido-ainu⟧. In early Japanese documents such as Ezo kotoba (1704), Matsumae no kotoba, and Ezoki (1795), the coda /r/ in *pirka* 'good' is predominantly written with the kana る (*ru*) or ル (*ru*), rather than り (*ri*) or リ (*ri*) ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-early-japanese-documents-such-as-ezo-kotoba⟧; in contrast, other words containing /ir/ such as *sirkunne* 'dark', *sir* 'land', and *kikir* 'bug' are consistently written in early Japanese documents with kana り (*ri*) or 里 (*ri*), never る (*ru*) ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-contrast-to-pirka-good-other-words-containing⟧. In the Edo-period text Ezo chiyaranke narabini jōrurigen, the Ainu syllable *tu* is transcribed with the kana sequence トウ, as in ヱホマトウ for *ehomatu* 'to be surprised at' ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-the-edo-period-text-ezo-chiyaranke-narabini⟧. The east-coast Sakhalin greeting form *iyankarahte* was already in use by at least the mid-17th century, as attested in Vries's 1643 logbook form *Jankarate* ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--the-east-coast-sakhalin-greeting-form-iyankarahte-was⟧. Tangiku and Ogiwara (2001) transcribed and translated an Ainu-language letter written in Cyrillic script sent by Sentoku Taroji to Bronisław Piłsudski ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--tangiku-and-ogiwara-2001-transcribed-and-translated-an⟧. Ainu was spoken in the Tsugaru region of Honshu well into early modern times, but no concrete vocabulary was recorded aside from personal names ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--ainu-was-spoken-in-the-tsugaru-region-of⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語には固有の文字体系が存在せず⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--no-indigenous-writing-system⟧、近代に入るまでアイヌ自身にはアイヌ語を文字で書き表す習慣はなく⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--until-modern-times-the-ainu-themselves-had-no⟧、アイヌの手によってアイヌ語の文章が記録されるようになるのは20世紀になってからである⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--ainu-language-texts-began-to-be-documented-by⟧。17世紀あるいは18世紀前半にまで遡る信頼できかつある程度の分量をもつアイヌ語資料はきわめて少ない⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--there-are-very-few-reliable-and-sizable-documents⟧。モレラによる1591年の記録にある2つの単語は、西洋の言語で記録された史上最古のアイヌ語単語である可能性が極めて高く⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--the-two-words-in-a-record-dated-1591⟧、同記録において*Ainomoxori*という表記はアイヌ語の*ainu mosir*（アイヌの国・土地）を表し⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-the-early-western-record-by-morera-1591⟧、*Rebuncur*という表記はアイヌ語の*repun kur*（海の向こうからの異邦人）を表している⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-the-early-western-record-by-morera-1591-2⟧。『松前ノ言葉』や『蝦夷言葉』のような日本の最初期のアイヌ語資料では、日本語と同様にアイヌ語も変体仮名を含む平仮名で書かれており⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-the-earliest-japanese-documents-of-ainu-such⟧、変体仮名の「川」(*tsu*)や「志」(*shi*)は日本語の表記よりもアイヌ語の表記において多く用いられている⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-early-japanese-documents-recording-ainu-the-hentaigana⟧。その後の江戸時代の文献では、日本語が一般に漢字と平仮名で書かれるのに対し、アイヌ語は片仮名で表記される傾向がある⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-later-edo-era-documents-ainu-tends-to⟧。ブガエワは、17世紀の『松前ノ言』における「ゆ王んふ（*yuwanfu*）」という表記から、現代アイヌ語の*iwanpe*「6」はかつて**iwanp*または**iwanpə*のような形であった可能性があると提案している⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--the-modern-ainu-form-iwanpe-six-may-historically⟧。現代アイヌ語において*okkay*は通常「成人男性」を意味するが、アンジェリスの記録や『松前ノ言』といった17世紀の資料では「若い男、少年」と説明されていた⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--whereas-okkay-in-modern-ainu-usually-means-adult⟧。18世紀初頭のアイヌ語における*hu*の発音は、現代の[ɸu]ではなく[hu]または[xu]であった⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-the-early-18th-century-the-ainu-pronunciation⟧。ブガエワは、『犾言葉』における「あへ連んほう（*aherenhou*）」という表記から、語根*rep*「炉の中心または海」がかつて**reHp*のように未知の子音**H*を含んでいた可能性があると提案している⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--the-root-rep-center-of-hearth-or-sea⟧。『蝦夷草紙』（1790年）では、音節/*tu*/を表記するために特殊な仮名文字「ト゜」が用いられている⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--ezo-s-shi-1790-employs-the-special-kana⟧。『松前の言』（17世紀）には、現代北海道アイヌ語の*réra*「風」に対する「連いら」（*reira*）や*téta*「ここ」に対する「てい多」（*teita*）など、現代北海道アイヌ語には存在しない長母音を示唆する表記が含まれている⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--matsumae-no-kotoba-17th-c-contains-kana-spellings⟧。日本の古文書において、現代北海道アイヌ語の*tókap*「昼」は「とふかつふ」（*tofukatsufu*）や「トーガプ」（*toogapu*）のように第1音節の長音を示す仮名表記で頻繁に記録されている⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--old-japanese-documents-frequently-record-modern-hokkaido-ainu⟧。『蝦夷言葉』（1704年）、『松前の言』、『蝦夷記』（1795年）などの初期の文献において、*pirka*「良い」の末子音/r/は「り／リ」ではなく圧倒的に仮名「る／ル」で表記されている⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-early-japanese-documents-such-as-ezo-kotoba⟧が、*sirkunne*「暗い」、*sir*「大地」、*kikir*「虫」など/ir/を含む他の語は、初期文献において一貫して仮名「り／里」で書かれ、「る」で書かれることはない⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-contrast-to-pirka-good-other-words-containing⟧。江戸時代の文献『蝦夷談判並浄瑠璃言』において、アイヌ語の音節*tu*は*ehomatu*「驚く」を表す「ヱホマトウ」のように仮名「トウ」で書き表されている⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--in-the-edo-period-text-ezo-chiyaranke-narabini⟧。1643年のフリースの航海日誌にある*Jankarate*という記録から、樺太東海岸の挨拶言葉の形（*iyankarahte*）が少なくとも17世紀半ばには存在していたことがわかる⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--the-east-coast-sakhalin-greeting-form-iyankarahte-was⟧。丹菊・荻原（2001）は、千徳太郎次がピウスツキに書き送った、キリル文字によるアイヌ語の書簡を翻刻・和訳したものである⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--tangiku-and-ogiwara-2001-transcribed-and-translated-an⟧。津軽地方においては近世に入ってもアイヌ語が日常的に話されていたことが推測されているが、人名を除いて具体的な語例は記録されていない⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--ainu-was-spoken-in-the-tsugaru-region-of⟧。

text.en: The Ainu language has no indigenous writing system, and very few attempts have ever been made by speakers to compose written texts directly in Ainu ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--no-indigenous-writing-system⟧⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--very-few-attempts-have-ever-been-made-by⟧. There are very few reliable and sizable documents of the Ainu language dating back as far as the 17th century or the first half of the 18th century ⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--there-are-very-few-reliable-and-sizable-documents⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語には固有の文字体系が存在せず、アイヌ語で自ら書かれた文章を創作しようとする試みは極めて稀にしか行われてこなかった⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--no-indigenous-writing-system⟧⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--very-few-attempts-have-ever-been-made-by⟧。17世紀あるいは18世紀前半にまで遡る信頼できかつある程度の分量をもつアイヌ語資料はきわめて少ない⟦claim:sources/written-sources-grammars-dictionaries--there-are-very-few-reliable-and-sizable-documents⟧。
